rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufr means denying God's oneness; the source groups the same expression in al-Ḥajj and Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: الكفر الإنكار قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufr can mean denial after recognizing the truth; the entry gives an al-Anʿām parallel.
rows.anchor: الكفر الجحود قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufr means ingratitude, as in the commands to be thankful and not ungrateful; the source also cites 27:40 and 26:19.
rows.anchor: الكفر كفر النعمة قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufr means disavowal: Satan says he repudiated those whom people associated with God; parallels occur in al-ʿAnkabūt and al-Mumtaḥana.
rows.anchor: الكفر البراءة قوله تعالى في سورة إبراهيم عن إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kifl means a doubled share, here twofold mercy and reward.
rows.anchor: الكفل الضعف قوله تعالى في سورة الحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kifl can mean a burden of sin: the one who advocates evil shares its burden.
rows.anchor: الكفل الوزر قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kafala means to take responsibility for Mary's care; the related question in 3:44 means to undertake raising her.
rows.anchor: كفل أي ضمن قوله سبحانه في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kafala can mean nursing, as in the offer to find a household to nurse the child.
rows.anchor: الكفالة الرضاعة قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalām can mean God's speech heard by a servant directly, without an intermediary; the entry also cites 2:75.
rows.anchor: الكلام الذي أسمع الله تعالى عبده من غير واسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalām Allāh can mean the revealed Qur'an; the source gives the same sense for God's words in al-Fatḥ.
rows.anchor: كلام الله القرآن قوله سبحانه في سورة التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's words can mean His wonders; the entry links this sense to Luqmān 31:27.
rows.anchor: كلمات الله عجائبه تعالى قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source lists seven further senses of kalimāt: rites, what Adam received, words of tawḥīd, God's creative wonders, Jesus, God's religion, and the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ك ل م على سبعة أوجه المناسك ما تلقى آدم ألفاظ التوحيد عجائب صنع الله عيسى عليه السلام دين الله القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq can mean food given previously; the source compares the food Joseph's fellow prisoners are given.
rows.anchor: أي أطعمنا من قبل ونحوه كثير مثل قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq can refer specifically to morning and evening meals in Paradise.
rows.anchor: الرزق الغداء والعشاء خاصة قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq can mean gratitude, so the phrase means making one's thanks that one denies the truth.
rows.anchor: الرزق الشكر قوله تعالى في سورة الواقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq can mean rain.
rows.anchor: الرزق المطر قوله تعالى في سورة الذاريات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq can mean the maintenance owed to nursing mothers.
rows.anchor: الرزق النفقة قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the account of Mary, rizq means fruit from both winter and summer.
rows.anchor: الرزق بمعنى الفاكهة خاصة قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq can mean reward; the source also glosses the believers who are provided for after death as being rewarded.
rows.anchor: الرزق الثواب قوله تعالى في سورة الطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq can mean Paradise and its delights.
rows.anchor: الرزق بمعنى الجنة قوله تعالى في سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arsala can mean to empower: God has empowered the devils over the unbelievers; the source gives parallels in al-Muṭaffifīn and al-Qamar.
rows.anchor: أرسلنا سلطنا فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arsala can mean to send or commission someone as a messenger.
rows.anchor: أرسل أي بعث فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arsala can mean to open or release: none can open what God withholds.
rows.anchor: أرسل فتح قوله تعالى في سورة الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arsala can mean to bring out and make manifest, as with the she-camel; the source also cites 17:59.
rows.anchor: أرسل بمعنى أخرج وأظهر قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arsala can mean to dispatch or direct people; the source compares Joseph's brothers sending their water drawer.
rows.anchor: أرسل أي وجه قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arsala can mean to release people from punishment; Moses asks Pharaoh to release the Children of Israel, with parallels in al-Shuʿarāʾ and al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: أي أطلق من العذاب كقوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry's seventh listed sense of arsala is to send down.
rows.anchor: سلط بعث فتح أخرج وجه أطلق أنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalīl can mean nothing at all; the source illustrates this with phrases that mean people do not remember, believe, or give thanks at all.
rows.anchor: قليل يعني لا شيء قوله تعالى في سورة غافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalīl can mean few relative to a much larger group; the source says Moses had 600,000 followers and Pharaoh 700,000,000 companions.
rows.anchor: القليل في الكثير قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'few' who remained with Saul are identified as 313 men, also the number of the people at Badr.
rows.anchor: وثلاثة عشر وهم قوم طالوت وعدة أهل بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The small number who believed with Noah is identified as 80 people: 40 men and 40 women.
rows.anchor: القليل ثمانون نفسا أربعون رجلا وأربعون امرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The few who know the number of the Companions of the Cave are identified as ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: القليل عبد الله بن العباس قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqlām can mean arrows used for drawing lots: the people cast them into water to decide who would care for Mary.
rows.anchor: الأقلام السهام قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalam can also mean the writing instrument itself, by which writing is made.
rows.anchor: القلم بعينه قوله تعالى في سورة ن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qānitūn can mean those who acknowledge God's lordship and servitude; the source gives a parallel in al-Rūm.
rows.anchor: قانتون أي مقرون بالعبودية قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qānitūn can mean obedient, as in the command to stand obediently in prayer; the source also cites al-Aḥzāb.
rows.anchor: قانتون مطيعون قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqāma can mean to acknowledge prayer without actually believing it; the source cites the same phrase again in al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: إقرار من غير تصديق قوله تعالى في سورة براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqāma can mean to complete or perform prayer; the source gives many parallels, including al-Baqara and al-Mujādila.
rows.anchor: يعني يتمونها في سورة البقرة والمجادلة وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The six listed senses of q-w-m include completing, facing, purifying, doing or showing, setting upright, and settling; the explained first sense is completion.
rows.anchor: ق وم على ستة أوجه أتم استقبل أخلص عمل به أو بينه نصبه استوطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Liqāʾ can mean meeting God, understood as resurrection after death and the reckoning; the source gives parallels in al-Furqān and al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: لقاء الله سبحانه وتعالى بمعنى البعث بعد الموت قوله تعالى في سورة يس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Liqāʾ can mean meeting the enemy in battle.
rows.anchor: اللقاء بمعنى الحرب والقتال قوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Liqāʾ can mean seeing: the phrase means when they saw the believers; the source also cites al-Aḥzāb and two other verses in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: اللقاء الرؤية قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Liqāʾ can mean being given something; patience is given only to the steadfast, and the source cites 76:11.
rows.anchor: اللقاء العطاء قوله سبحانه في سورة حم السجدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Liqāʾ can mean descending or coming upon someone: death will inevitably come upon the people who flee from it.
rows.anchor: اللقاء النزول قوله سبحانه في سورة الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alqā can mean to whisper; Satan whispered into the recitation.
rows.anchor: ألقى وسوس قوله تعالى في سورة الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alqā can mean to create, as in God's creating mountains on earth; the source also cites Qāf.
rows.anchor: ألقى أي خلق قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alqā can mean to place something somewhere; the source also cites the messenger placing Joseph's shirt on his father's face.
rows.anchor: ألقى أي وضع قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alqā can mean to send down; the source uses it of sending revelation and cites al-Mursalāt and al-Muzzammil.
rows.anchor: ألقى بمعنى أنزل قوله تعالى في سورة حم المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alqā can mean to draw lots, as when the people cast their pens to decide who would care for Mary.
rows.anchor: إذ يقلون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alqā can mean to clothe: God says He clothed Moses with beauty and bestowed it upon his brother.
rows.anchor: ألقي بمعني كسا كقوله تعالى في سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alqā can mean to put someone into the Fire; the source compares the command to cast someone into Hell.
rows.anchor: ألقي بمعني أدخل قوله تعالى في سورة فصلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten listed senses of alqā include whispering, creating, placing, sending down, drawing lots, clothing, entering, throwing, speaking, and seating; this excerpt explains the first seven.
rows.anchor: ل ق ى على عشرة أوجه وسوس خلق وضع أنزل أقرع كسا أدخل رمى كلم أجلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna can express what is proper or fitting: it is not fitting for a person given scripture and prophecy to ask people to worship him.
rows.anchor: كان بمعنى ينبغي قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna can be an extra connective with no added meaning, so the phrase means simply 'God is knowing and wise.'
rows.anchor: كان صلة في الكلام قوله تعالى في سورة الأحزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna can mean 'he is' or 'he was,' as in the question about the child in the cradle.
rows.anchor: كان يعني هو قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

words: وكان الله على كل شيء قديرا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna can function as an explanatory form equivalent to 'God is capable of everything'; the source groups examples from al-Aḥzāb, al-Fatḥ, and Maryam.
rows.anchor: وكان رسولا نبيا وكان يأمر أهله بالصلاة والزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna can mean 'became'; the source gives examples of the sky becoming openings and the sky and mountains changing form.
rows.anchor: كان يعني صار قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd can mean punishment: God's plan against the deniers is a severe punishment.
rows.anchor: الكيد العذاب قوله سبحانه في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd can mean killing; the source says the unbelievers intended to kill the Prophet and were killed at Badr.
rows.anchor: الكيد القتل قوله تعالى في سورة الطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd can mean plotting or guile, as in Joseph asking to be protected from the women's scheme.
rows.anchor: الكيد المكر قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd can mean a stratagem or device: the challenge is to use whatever device one has.
rows.anchor: الكيد الحيلة قوله تعالى في المرسلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd can mean making or contriving; the source explains the phrase as doing a deed and connects it to the killing planned at Badr.
rows.anchor: الكيد الصنع قوله تعالى في سورة طارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd can mean burning in fire, as the people intended to burn Abraham.
rows.anchor: الكيد الحرق بالنار قوله تعالى في سورة الصافات والأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd can mean strangling: the verse asks whether his strangling will remove what enrages him.
rows.anchor: الكيد الخنق قوله تعالى في سورة الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aslama can mean to make one's religion sincere for God; the source also applies that sense to 3:20 and 31:22.
rows.anchor: يقول أخلص قال أخلصت وقال تعالى

words: وَلَهُۥٓ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aslama can mean to acknowledge servitude to God; the source compares the verbal profession in al-Ḥujurāt and a profession without sincere faith in al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: الإسلام يعني الإقرار قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Silm can mean peace or reconciliation; the source also cites the instruction not to reject an offer of peace in al-Nisāʾ.
rows.anchor: السلم يعني الصلح قوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-silm in the call to enter it all together refers to the law of the Prophet Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: السلم شريعة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Salām is one of God's names; the source also interprets 'the paths of peace' and 'the abode of peace' as referring to God.
rows.anchor: السلام الله تعالى قوله تعالى في سورة الحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salām can mean good words or goodwill, as in the replies to the ignorant and the greeting to Abraham's father; the source also cites Hūd.
rows.anchor: السلام يعني الخير قوله تعالى في سورة الزخرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salām can mean praise; the source identifies the praise in this verse as being for Moses and Aaron.
rows.anchor: السلام يعني الثناء الحسن قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salām can mean safety from harm; the source also reads it as safety in the greeting to the people of the right and God's command to the fire.
rows.anchor: السلام يعني السلامة من الشر قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry lists greeting as a fifth sense of salām, alongside God's name, good, praise, and safety.
rows.anchor: س ل م على خمسة أوجه الله تعالى الخير الثناء الحسن السلامة التحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first disbeliever means the first person among the Jews of Medina to disbelieve in the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أول يعني من كفر بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awwal can designate the first person in Mecca to believe in God; the source links it with the first Muslims in al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: أول يعني أول من آمن بالله تعالى من أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source says Moses was the first to know and affirm that God cannot be seen in this world.
rows.anchor: أول من عرف إن الله تعالى لا يرى في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians' phrase means that they were the first believers among the Children of Israel in Moses and Aaron.
rows.anchor: أول المؤمنين من بني إسرائيل بموسى وهرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl can mean the extent of Muhammad's and his community's reign; the source says Jews sought to calculate when it would end through abjad letter values, but only God knows it.
rows.anchor: متى ينقضي ملكه ويعود إليهم . قال الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl can mean the outcome of what God promised through the Messenger in the Qur'an, good or evil, realized on Resurrection; the source gives parallel verses.
rows.anchor: التأويل بمعنى ما وعد الله تعالى في القرآن على لسان الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry lists five senses of taʾwīl—kingship, outcome, dream interpretation, color, and verification—but this segment explains only the first two.
rows.anchor: الملك . العاقبة . تعبير الرؤيا . اللون . التحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs can mean the heart; the source also glosses what is within a person in al-Isrāʾ as the heart.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى في سورة ق ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anfus can mean 'among you' or 'from your own people,' as in the description of the Messenger.
rows.anchor: الثاني من أنفسكم أي منكم قوله تعالى في سورة براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs can mean a human being, as in the rule of a life for a life.
rows.anchor: النفس الإنسان قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anfus can mean one another: the command means that some of the people should kill others among them.
rows.anchor: اقتلوا أنفسكم أي ليقتل بعضكم بعضا قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs can mean the soul or spirit; the source also cites God's taking the souls at death.
rows.anchor: النفس الروح قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anfus can mean members of one's religious community, so the prohibition includes killing fellow believers.
rows.anchor: أنفسكم أي أهل دينكم قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs can mean a person's whole self or being, in the command that each person kill himself.
rows.anchor: نفس الإنسان جملته قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs can mean punishment: God warns people of His punishment.
rows.anchor: النفس العقوبة قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anfus can mean mothers; the source interprets the phrase as thinking well of their mothers.
rows.anchor: النفس الأم قوله تعالى في سورة النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs can mean the unseen or inner reality: Jesus says that God knows his unseen and he does not know God's.
rows.anchor: النفس الغيب قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infāq can mean paying zakāt.
rows.anchor: النفقة الزكاة قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infāq can mean giving charity; the source also cites 57:7 and 63:10.
rows.anchor: النفقة الصدقة قوله تعالى في سور آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infāq can mean spending in support of God's religion, including the religious cause and military effort; the source cites 57:10.
rows.anchor: النفقة البذل في نصرة الدين قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infāq can mean maintenance spent on wives.
rows.anchor: النفقة على الزوجات قوله تعالى في سورة الطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infāq can mean spending on construction or cultivation, as in the ruined garden.
rows.anchor: النفقة العمارة قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infāq can mean poverty or fear of becoming poor.
rows.anchor: الانفاق الفقر قوله سبحانه في سورة الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infāq can mean providing sustenance: God provides as He wills; the source says the root meaning is whatever a person spends from his wealth in any way.
rows.anchor: الانفاق الرزق قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source states that the basic sense of nafaqa is whatever a person spends from his wealth in any way.
rows.anchor: وأصل النفقة ما أخرجه الإنسان من ماله على الوجوه كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqīb can mean a trustworthy representative or witness.
rows.anchor: النقيب الأمين قوله سبحانه في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqqabū can mean to travel or roam through the lands.
rows.anchor: فنقبوا أي طافوا قوله تعالى في سورة ق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nikāḥ can mean marriage; the source gives examples in al-Nisāʾ and al-Nūr as well.
rows.anchor: النكاح التزويج قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nikāḥ can mean sexual intercourse, as in the condition that a woman have intercourse with another husband.
rows.anchor: النكاح الجماع قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istinkāḥ can mean taking the woman who offers herself as a wife; the source says this dispensation applies only to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: النكاح الهبة قوله تعالى في سورة الأحزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nikāḥ can mean puberty or sexual maturity.
rows.anchor: النكاح الحلم قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahr can mean springs or water sources.
rows.anchor: الأنهار الأعين قوله تعالى في سورة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahr can mean a flowing stream in a garden.
rows.anchor: النهر هو الجاري في البساتين قوله تعالى في نظائر كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahr can refer specifically to the Jordan River in Palestine.
rows.anchor: النهر نهر الأردن وفلسطين قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahr can mean spaciousness or abundance.
rows.anchor: النهر السعة قوله تعالى في سورة القمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry's five-face list also names an unexplained fifth label, غار.
rows.anchor: ن ه ر على خمسة أوجه العين الجاري في البستان نهر الأردن وفلسطين السعة غار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asrār can mean concealment or secrecy; the source also contrasts secret and public giving in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: السر الإخفاء قوله تعالى في سورة الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarīʿ al-ḥisāb can mean that the reckoning has arrived; the source gives a parallel in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: سريع يعني مجيء الحساب قوله سبحانه في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarīʿ al-ḥisāb can mean quick to finish the reckoning once it begins; the source cites al-Anʿām and reports a half-day duration from Ibn ʿAbbās through Muqātil.
rows.anchor: سريع الحساب أي سريع الفراغ من الحساب إذا أخذ فيه

rows.speaker: مقاتل عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Muqātil reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that God completes the creatures' reckoning in half a day by the reckoning of worldly days, so the people of Paradise rest in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل عن ابن عباس : يفرغ الله من حساب الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isrāf can mean unlawfully taking the property of orphans.
rows.anchor: الإسراف بمعنى الحرام قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isrāf can mean exceeding what is due: the prohibition means not killing anyone other than the killer.
rows.anchor: الإسلام يعني خلاف ما يجب قوله تعالى في سورة الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isrāf can mean spending on disobedience; the source says the balanced spenders do not spend on sin.
rows.anchor: الإسراف النفقة في المعصية قوله تعالى في سورة الفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isrāf can mean declaring lawful things forbidden; the source links the prohibition to 6:141 as well.
rows.anchor: الإسراف يعني تحريم الحلال قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-musrifīn can refer to those who associate partners with God.
rows.anchor: الإسراف الإشراك بالله تعالى قوله عز وجل في سورة حم المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asrafū can mean going to excess and committing many sins.
rows.anchor: الإسراف الإفراط في المعاصي والإكثار منها قوله تعالى في سورة الزمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿy has three listed senses—walking, action, and haste; the explained sense is walking, with examples from al-Baqara, al-Ṣāffāt, and al-Jumuʿa.
rows.anchor: السعي المشي قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة
